about.title: San Mateo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Most drives across San Mateo are uneventful, right up until one isn't. In 2025, the city logged 386 injury collisions, and 529 people were hurt in them; four of those crashes were fatal. Public records show reports clustering on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., which tracks with the commute flow along US-101, S El Camino Real, and SR-92. Those corridors simply carry a lot of traffic, and volume brings collisions. If you were injured in one of them, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. LawProactive exists to make one part simpler. Tell us what happened, and we connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles San Mateo County car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing unless there is a recovery. Before you speak with the other driver's insurer, it helps to have someone in your corner who knows what a fair claim looks like and what evidence needs to be saved right now.

whyChoose.title: Why San Mateo Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than People Expect
items.desc: California allows two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle or road condition is involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting connected early keeps those options open.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for a collision on SR-92 or El Camino Real; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate that percentage.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Fee
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is nothing to pay unless your case results in a recovery. They will also handle the other insurer for you, which means you are not pressured into a recorded statement that can be used to shrink your claim.

items.question: I was hit on US-101 near San Mateo and the other driver's insurer keeps calling. Do I have to give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and it is generally wise not to until you have talked with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be framed as admissions. Politely decline, save the claim number, and let LawProactive connect you with someone who can take over that conversation.

items.question: What evidence should I hold onto after a San Mateo car accident?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the roadway, and your injuries, along with the police report number from San Mateo Police or CHP. Save medical records, receipts, and any texts or emails from insurers. If your crash happened at a busy spot like S El Camino Real, nearby businesses may have camera footage that gets overwritten quickly, so acting within days matters.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive, and what if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: LawProactive is free to use, and the independent attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California's pure comparative fault system lets you pursue a claim even when you share some responsibility. Your compensation is reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case.
